caption:
OpenAI has bought Odessia, an AI travel agent that books flights and hotels by text.
The service opened to the public on October 14 and was switched off once the deal was announced.
Expedia shares fell as much as 5% on the news.

Would you let ChatGPT book your next trip?

site_article.headline: OpenAI acquires AI travel agent Odessia and shuts down its service
site_article.dek: The text-based travel concierge from Sonder founder Francis Davidson had opened to the public less than a month earlier.
site_article.summary: OpenAI has acquired Odessia, an AI travel agent founded by Sonder co-founder Francis Davidson, and the standalone service has closed. Expedia shares fell as much as 5% on the day of the announcement, according to The Next Web.
site_article.seo_title: OpenAI acquires Odessia AI travel agent, shuts its service
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI bought Odessia, the AI travel agent from Sonder founder Francis Davidson, and closed the service. Expedia and Booking shares fell on the news.
site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI acquired Odessia, an AI travel agent that booked flights and hotels by text, on November 10, 2026. Terms were not disclosed, the service has closed, and founder Francis Davidson is joining OpenAI to work on travel.
site_article.hero_alt: A smartphone and a computer screen both showing the OpenAI logo.

paragraphs.text: Francis Davidson, the founder of the AI travel agent Odessia, said on November 10, 2026 that OpenAI has acquired his company. Davidson announced the deal in a post on X, and the terms were not disclosed, according to TechCrunch and Skift.

Odessia's standalone service has already closed. The Next Web reported that the service was shut down the same day the acquisition was announced, and that the company's website now says the service is no longer available. Odessia had opened to the public on October 14, 2026, less than a month earlier.

Odessia worked as a travel concierge that customers reached by text message. According to The Next Web, it planned and booked flights, hotels and complete itineraries within a single conversation, and it ran on OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and Codex models.

The company held IATA accreditation, which let it issue airline tickets and book directly as a travel agent. Tbreak reported that it could read booking confirmations in a user's Gmail account to learn travel preferences, and that it offered private hotel rates with perks such as breakfast and upgrades at about 2,000 hotels.

Davidson said tens of thousands of early users tried the service over the summer and planned more than $60 million a year in travel with it. That figure describes planned travel, not revenue, and it comes from Davidson himself. Travelers with existing bookings are being directed to Odessia's support email, according to tbreak.

Odessia was about a year old and had a team of roughly eight people in San Francisco. It raised about $6 million in a round led by Sequoia Capital, which was announced in June 2026, according to Skift and TechCrunch.

OpenAI did not announce the acquisition itself, and TechCrunch said the company did not confirm the deal when asked. TechCrunch described the transaction as looking like an acqui-hire. The Next Web quoted an OpenAI spokesperson describing Davidson as a proven founder who has built several businesses that help people travel.

Davidson said he is joining OpenAI to work on the future of travel. OpenAI has not announced any travel products or plans. TechCrunch noted that when OpenAI launched ChatGPT agent in July 2025, it named travel as one of the possible uses.

The news reached the stock market. The Next Web, citing Investing.com, reported that Expedia shares fell as much as 5% on Tuesday, Booking Holdings as much as 3% and Airbnb around 3.5%. Several of those companies already work with OpenAI: Booking.com and Expedia were among the first travel platforms to put their apps inside ChatGPT.

Davidson co-founded Sonder, an apartment hotel company, in 2014 while he was still a student. Sonder went public through a SPAC, later lost a key partnership with Marriott, and went bankrupt before winding down. Davidson resigned as Sonder's chief executive in June 2025, according to TechCrunch.

TechCrunch reported that Davidson's announcement focused mostly on how he built Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The Next Web said he described a working style in which a very small team leaned heavily on agents to build the product.

For NeuraFeed, the notable part is the speed. A travel agent built on OpenAI's own models opened to everyone in mid-October and was folded into OpenAI within four weeks. The share moves suggest investors see a risk that ChatGPT could one day book trips directly instead of sending users to online travel agencies, even though OpenAI has said nothing about its plans.
The next signal to watch is whether ChatGPT gains a built-in way to plan and pay for trips, and how Expedia and Booking Holdings describe their OpenAI partnerships in their next earnings calls.
